properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/22/2024 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/22/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8198932
Permit API: 117-22210
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/22/2024
Comments: On 8/22/2024 at 1100 hrs., Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event Inspection (INCDT) of the Seneca Resources - Bauer 849 well pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. Complaint Id: 383218. It was 66 and partly cloudy when I arrived at the site.When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's company man, Adam Pierce. Adam explained current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet is on site performing stimulation operations on seven recently drilled wells. The crew is currently zippering between 64HU, 66HU and 67HU wells with the other four wells already completed. Adam expects the crew to be done fracking the wells by August 24, 2024.Adam showed me where the spill event occurred. Tighe Truman joined us during the inspection. A water hauling truck like the one shown in pictures 3, 4 and 5 was backed up to the frac tanks located along the south edge of the pad. The truck driver was running the on-board air pump to provide air pressure to help push the liquids out of the tank. While the water truck was pressuring up, a pop-off valve valve that was connected to the top hatch on the front of the tank released pressure and released an estimated 20 gallons of produced water from the tank, the liquids impacting the ground under the truck and flowing a short distance east. The truck driver was at the controls on the side of the truck and immediately stopped pressuring the truck. Normally the pop-off valve should be above the fluid level but the front wheels of the truck were parked in a small depression that allowed the level of fluid to be above the pop-off connection. Discussing this incident with Adam and Tighe, the normal operating pressure is unknown and the pressure that the pop-off released at is unknown. It was unknown at the time of this inspection if the valve failed and opened below the designed relief pressure or if the driver allowed the pressure in the tank to exceed the designed pop-off relief pressure. Adam did say that it was a new driver and believes that the driver did not open the discharge valve on the truck before applying pressure. Adam commented that with the small air pocket of a fully loaded truck, it would only take a short amount of time to build up pressure. The area of the release is shown in pictures 3 and 6. The surface of the area has been scraped and new gravel has been installed. The scraped material was placed into a rolloff dumpster that, due to a previous spill, was already stationed at the site. The dumpster is lined and staged in secondary containment. Water in the truck offloading catch basin field tested at 11.06 mS conductance. Water in the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 19.49 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance liquids with Adam who said that he would have employees continue cleaning out the containments.The release of well-bore fluids to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402(b) and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Discuss with the trucking company the need to inspect the equipment involved with this incident to ensure it is in serviceable condition. The pop-off valve should be examined to determine if it operated correctly or failed. Remove/repair equipment as necessary.2. Ensure personnel are trained on the safe and proper procedure for offloading fluids from tanker trucks.3. Screen the area impacted by the release of well-bore fluids for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.4. Continue to remove the elevated conductance fluid from the frac tank secondary containment and the unloading catch basin. Train personnel on proper procedures to prevent releasing the elevated conductance fluids into the containments. I left the site at 1230 hours.

Report Details

Violation ID: 990004
Permit API: 015-23753
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/30/2023
Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 25 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested some of these with an Oakton PCTS 50 for conductivity and discovered a 60' x 60' ice/water puddle southeast of the wellheads and adjacent to the south edge of the secondary containment for six frac tanks that field tested at 4.05 mS conductance. Sample 9551-049 was collected from this puddle. Two water puddles between the two frac tank secondary containments field tested at 1.5 mS conductance. Other water puddles tested at less than 0.6 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance fluids with Chesapeake's Kyle Stephens. He directed an arriving vac truck to start sucking up the fluids. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization has been applied to the perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place down slope from the infiltration areas.There were five wells staged for flowback/production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks in secondary containment that were connected to the wellheads. There were 10 frac tanks on the north side of location that were stationed in secondary containment but were not connected to the well heads at the time of the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface while cleaning up after fracking operations were completed and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.The release of a large volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402[b)The DEP recommends the following:1. Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.2. Continue to monitor the areas with temporary stabilization and apply addition resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 1010 hours.

Comments: On May 19, 2020, I conducted an inspection of the Vivian Harbison well site in Nottingham Township, Washington County. The inspection was a follow up inspection conducted in response to a fluid release reported to the Department on May 13, 2020 (See SAIR 3033281). The following was observed: Five roll off disposal boxes were staged on the well pad(photo#1). The disposal boxes were labeled as non-hazardous waste with a comment including stone and produced water (photo #2). The impacted area was surrounded with yellow caution tape. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 30' wide and 50' in length. Well pad material (stone) had been removed to an approximate depth of 3.5'. The impacted area stretches along the backside of multiple GPUs. The GPUs did not appear to be equipped with secondary containment. The GPUs appeared to be placed on a series of steel plates. The individual plates did not appear to be welded together (photo #3). I utilized a Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to collect conductivity readings in and around the impacted area and between the GPUs. The following readings were collected. Behind GPU 592605A, I collected a reading of 8.18 mS under the steel plate (photo#4). I observed a puddle of fluid on the steel plate between GPU 592604A and 592605A, I collected a reading of 12.95 mS. The area was covered with what appeared to be wood chips. I detected conductivity in excess of the reading limit of the unit within the wood chip area the result was Or. The maximum limit of the unit is 20 mS. (photo #5,6,9,10,11, and 12) At GPU 592603A, I collected a reading of 7.51 mS (photo #7 and 8). Based on the observations made during this inspection it does not appear that the Operator has removed the impacted material from the well pad. The GPUs are not equipped with secondary containment and the GPUs may need to be removed to accomplish remediation activity. Violations remain outstanding and new violations are being issued based on the observations made during this inspection.

Violation ID: 8241087
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 7/14/2025
Comments: At 1945 hours on 7/13/2025, the Department received notification of a well control incident at the Broadleaf Holdings 7H unconventional gas well. Reportedly, Repsol personnel observed fluids from the well overtopping containment while stimulating the well. The purpose of this Administrative inspection report is to document the Department's initial response to the notification using the SubSAIR mobile app. In response to the notification, the Department deployed Emergency Response Team (ERT) members Jonathan Pennings and Scotty Brown to the site. Jonathan Pennings arrived at 2135 hours on 7/13/2025 and Scotty Brown arrived at 2058 hours on 7/13/2025. Upon arrival, an unknown amount of fluids was observed outside of containment. During the initial response, booms were deployed and earthen berms were constructed in an attempt to mitigate runoff. Reportedly, "halfway through the frac," the well pressure dropped from approximately 9000 psi to 3000 psi and all three annuli were compromised leading to a fluids release from the well to the surface. Further inquiry revealed that the breach occurred while stimulating Stage 50 of 67 at approximately 18:05 hours. In response, Repsol attempted to set a kill plug below the breach, but the plug got stuck near surface. At that time, it was determined the a Coil Tubing Unit would be necessary to drill out the stuck plug and set a new kill plug. Reportedly, no combustible gas was detected at this time. At 01:15 hours on 7/14/2025, CUDD Well Control (CUDD) and Mansfield Crane arrive to the site. At 0331, CUDD setup water cannons for safety purposes. Water management efforts continued on the pad. At 0900 on 7/14/2025, Kyle Menc (Oil and Gas Inspector) arrived to the site to continue the Department's oversight efforts. Jonathan Pennings left the site at 0640 hours on 7/14/2025 and Scotty Brown left the site at 0930 hours on 7/14/2025. Additional details regarding the Department's initial response to the notification are provided in the PADEP-Emergency Response Incident Report generated by Scotty Brown. Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from DCNR that a hunter believed that there was a possible brine discharge from this location. The email was forwarded on 11/18/22, and it had been brought to the operator's attention on 11/17.It appears as though a brine leak has occurred sometime between DEP's 4/20/22 inspection and now. It is uncertain which tank the leak is emanating from, as the containment has been compromised and deer tracks are evident throughout.Some volume of brine has leached through the soil and come out on the east side of the containment on the edge of a swale. Significant deer activity has occurred at this point, causing rutting and erosion on the bank of the containment. Conductivity over 1 mS was noted with a meter at several points in the soil. The swale is currently running water, with slightly elevated conductivity noted in the water. As such, it is clear that brine discharge has occurred.The operator was contacted and stated that they would have someone visit the site on 11/30 to inspect, and would begin remediation after. Followup inspection will be done as necessary.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to being notified of a crude oil release at a tank battery located approximately 400 feet northeast of this conventional well.Equipment failure during sub freezing temperatures resulted in a release of crude oil within the earthen containment that surrounds two 210 bbl stock tanks. A majority of the product remained inside of the containment, however a de minimis amount was observed in the roadside ditch adjacent to the tank battery. Pennhills has placed absorbent diapers in the ditch and installed an underflow dam in the ditch, approximately 150 feet downslope of the tank battery. Pennhills intends to regularly vac out the residual product that remains inside of the containment and maintain/monitor the containment measures in the ditch.At this time, the current remediation efforts appear sufficient, additional inspections will be conducted throughout and after the spring thaw to evaluate if additional measures are justified.

Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8167305
Permit API: 125-23364
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/30/2023
Comments: On 11/30/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Stech F69 well. The following was observed:The well and operator's information were posted onsite (Photos 1, 2).The wellhead, production equipment, and production tank were in generally good condition. Some corrosion noted, loose wires/equipment near wellhead (Photos 3-6). Tank fluids high - I recommend pumping fluid out and placing lid on tank (Photo 7).Silt fence in the woods below production tank. I recommend ensuring that no sediment from the site washes downslope towards the tributary below (Photo 8).The access road was in poor condition leading the whole way to the site from the main road (Photos 9-25 with specific locations). Several areas displayed lack of maintenence and drainage concerns seen by pooling, potholes, channelization, and accelerated erosion. Culverts that run under the road leading to tributary to Pigeon Creek appeared to require clean out and outlet protection - erosion at outlets. There was a section of the access road closer to the entrance gate that displayed undercutting and failure along the guardrail. The integrity of the access road appeared jeopardized and may progress with repeated rain events and heavy truck traffic. The road does not display a safe way for emergency vehicles to navigate in case of emergency at the wellsite.Observations communicated to operator via phone on 11/30/23.Due to the poor condition of the access road and lack of maintenance, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78.53, and 102.22(a)2ii are being issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-12-26 to Coastal Petro Corp in Jenks Twp, Forest county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Coastal Petro Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-28
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 872750
Permit API: 053-30696
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-12-26
Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. A follow-up inspection found that the liquid crude oil/water mix that was in the secondary containment has been removed. There is ice and snow covering most of the bottom of the secondary containment making it unclear as to the extent of the clean-up however the ice around the tanks appears to be clear and does not contain any residual oil contamination. An empty plastic 200 gallon is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. A follow-up inspection will be completed when there is a thaw and the stone in the secondary containment can be inspected for contamination. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/26/2026 to BIG DOG ENERGY LLC in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland county. 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BIG DOG ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/26/2026
Violation Code: 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
Violation ID: 8286531
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/26/2026
Comments: On 8/26/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4237718, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. At the time of this inspection, no formal NOV Response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. Since the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. Since the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks. On 4/02/2026, Big Dog Energy representative Matthew Anderson responded via email to IR 4168852 and stated "As the DEP is aware this well was sold to Murphy Production in 2024. However in regards to the spill there was none. I ordered a new sign to put up just so this well can be transferred along with an ERP plan. Should have it within a week to install and get transferred to Murphy" (IR 4174382). However, the well site remained unchanged at the time of the previous inspection surface inspection, which was conducted on 7/15/2026 (IR 4237718).At the time of inspection, the following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (Photo 1). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (Photos 9 and 11). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (Photos 4-7). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (Photo 8). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (Photo 10). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (Photos 2 and 12).Based on todays inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4187078 remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken on site since the date of that inspection and no formal NOV Response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.
